, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the order 17.01.2014, passed in MVC No.109/2011 and MVC No.110/2011, by the Court of Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and CJM and Addl. MACT-II at Bidar, the claimants are before this Court.
The Court below had disposed off both the cases by way of a common order.
Hence this Court is also disposing of both these appeals by way of common order.
MFA No.201009/2014 arising out of MVC No.109/2011:
2. In this case claimant is 5 years old minor girl.

The compensation claimed is an amount of Rs.1,42,500/-
NC: 2024:KHC-K:630 for the injuries sustained by the claimant.
Immediately after the accident she took first aid treatment at Zahirabad and was inpatient from 05.04.2011 till 12.04.2011 in Gurunanak Hospital at Bidar.
She took follow up treatment as per the advise of the doctor.
In spite of that she was suffering from pain, discomfort and unable to attend her regular course of studies in a proper manner.
It is stated that she had spent an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards the treatment.
When it comes to the liability it is the case of the insurance company that the policy is an act policy and the claimant being the inmate of the car is not covered by the act policy.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

The Court below had observed that except the wound certificate and Ex.P2 the disability certificate no other document is placed before the Court Rehana Begum W/O Abdul Majeed vs Nizam Khan S/O Yasin Khan And Ors on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38572550/
3 and as per the wound certificate the claimant had sustained only simple injury that is abrasion on left Orbital area of her head and as per Ex.P2 she had taken treatment from 06.04.2011 till 12.04.2011.

sentences.text: The Court below also observed that the claimant had spent an NC: 2024:KHC-K:630 amount of Rs.4,425/- i.e. Ex.P3 to 6, 9 and 10 had granted an amount of Rs.7,500/- as compensation.

When it comes to the liability as it is an act policy, the Court below has held that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation and the owner was directed to pay the compensation.
3.
The learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that in this case the claimant is a 5 years old girl and she had sustained injury and had been a inpatient for sometime.
All these aspects were not considered by the Court below and granted a very meager compensation of Rs.7,500/-.
He submits that they have filed the cash receipt for the treatment and also for the purchase of the medicines.
These aspects were not appreciated by the Court below.
He submits that the Court went wrong in observing that the owner of the vehicle is alone liable to pay the compensation.
He submits that as there is an effective insurance policy, insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.
Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that the Court below had rightly exonerated the insurance company as it is an act policy.

He submits that as per the terms and conditions of the policy and as per the settled law, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation for any of the bodily injury to the inmates of the vehicle.
5. Though notice is served on the owner of the vehicle, there is no representation on behalf of the owner of the vehicle.

6. In this case, there is no dispute about the fact that the injured is a five years old who had sustained injuries and she was in hospital for about 6 days and also an admitted fact that all the reports were not filed before the Court below.

Considering the injury sustained by the claimant, the hospitalization and considering the age, this court is granting an amount of Rs.25,000/- globally when it comes to the liability the policy is a 'Act Policy' and the NC: 2024:KHC-K:630 court below rightly held that the owner alone is liable to pay the compensation.
Accordingly, appeal is partly allowed by granting an amount of Rs.25,000/-.
The owner alone is liable to pay the compensation.
MFA No.201008/2014 arising out of MVC NO.110/2011 7
. In this claimant is 40 years old and had suffered grievous injuries.
He claimed compensation of an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- and Court below had granted an amount of Rs.6,900/-.

It is the case of the claimant that immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Zahirabad Hospital and then came to Bidar Gurunanak Hospital wherein she took treatment as an inpatient from 05.04.2011 to 12.04.2011.
As per the advise of the doctor she took the follow up treatment.
She is constantly under pain and discomfort.
She was working as a Tailor and because of the injury sustained by her.
She has also sustained disability.

It is stated that she had spent an amount of more than Rs.90,000/-
towards medical NC: 2024:KHC-K:630 expenses.
She is unable to attain her routine course of work.

All these aspects were not considered by the Court below and granted a very meager compensation of an amount of Rs.6,900/-.
He submits that they have filed the cash receipt for the treatment and also purchase of the medicine.
These aspects were not appreciated by the Court below.
He submits that the Court went wrong in observing that the owner of the vehicle is alone liable to pay the compensation.
He submits that as there is an effective policy the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
9. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that the Court below had rightly exonerated the insurance company as it is an act policy.

NC: 2024:KHC-K:630 He submits that as per the terms and conditions of the policy and as per the settled law, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation for any of the bodily injury to the inmates of the case.
10. Though notice is served on the owner of the vehicle, there is no representation on behalf of the owner of the vehicle.

11. In this case, there is no dispute about the fact that the injured is a 40 years old who had sustained injuries and she was in hospital for about 6 days and it is an admitted fact that all the reports were not filed before the Court below.
Considering the injury sustained by the claimant, the hospitalization and considering the age, this court is granting an amount of Rs.25,000/- globally which owner alone is liable to pay.
12. Accordingly, the MFA No.201009/2014 is Partly Allowed by awarding global compensation of Rs.25,000/-.

On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing any security.
iii) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
iv) No costs.
